The --fail gate evaluates, in order: hard floors on the safety metrics (DECISION recall / CONTRADICT precision / depth accuracy < 0.75 fail immediately), evaluated first and absolute, before any comparability check, so they still fire when the comparison is skipped; then comparability preconditions (config + gate-code hash + corpus hash mismatches SKIP the flip-table comparison mechanically); then the per-row FLIP TABLE vs baseline judged by a mid-p McNemar test (p<0.05, ~5+ net one-directional flips) counting only STABLE flips (unanimous across BENCH_RUNS=3 majority-vote trials for detect/depth; retry-confirmed 2-of-2 for alignment), which requires a comparable baseline. --fail with no baseline exits NON-ZERO: 'cannot verify' is not 'verified fine'. Aggregate deltas print as informational only; every metric ships raw counts + a Wilson 95% interval plus an MDE line; every run appends to the runs.log ledger and post-fix rows enter as holdout.

Every completed row is appended to a gitignored progress-<sub>.jsonl the moment it lands, and re-running the SAME command replays those rows for free. A row is replayed only when config (model/K/cascade) AND gateHash AND corpusHash all match, so a stale checkpoint is inert rather than quietly blending two measurements; outage verdicts (NULL) are never replayed. Cost and stability aggregates are derived from the ROWS (per-row inputChars/rawChars/judged/outage) rather than counters incremented in the loop, so a resumed run reports what the whole run cost. The reader drops torn trailing lines instead of failing the load. --fresh discards and re-measures. An arm selected by an environment flag rather than a source edit is invisible to gateHash and corpusHash, so any bench that gains such an arm must either partition its checkpoint filename by that arm or extend its replay predicate to include the arm.

Markdown structure is read by mdast-util-from-markdown in one module (gate-engine/decisions/recall/markdown.mts), which is the only place permitted to know markdown layout. A section is 'this heading until the next heading', read off parser node offsets rather than inferred, so a boundary cannot be half-right. Retrieval consumes sections(); sliceToNextHeading, upToFirstNote and every lastIndexOf offset walk are deleted. Frontmatter stays hand-rolled — it parses exactly the two documented fields.

Lens holes are MEASURED before any lens is added, with one reusable reducer (external/holes.mts): a second detector's labelled findings are joined to what the correctness reviewer held in scope, saw in full, and said on the same change, and every miss is partitioned not-reviewed / not-in-scope / evidence-uncertain / in-evidence-unmatched / matched BEFORE any lens attribution. CodeRabbit categories on devkit's own repos are the primary instrument ($0, 100% marker parse, verification-trace roots dropped); Martian Code Review Bench goldens are a confirmatory external precision/recall probe and a source of miss candidates only. Only in-evidence-unmatched misses feed the lens question; attribution uses a pre-registered rubric (the four brief definitions plus an explicit none) whose light-judge triage must reach kappa >= 0.6 against hand labels before its column counts. A fifth lens is warranted only when a class no existing checklist names holds a clear majority of eligible misses (category denominator >= 8 catchable) across both sources AND a prompt-bullet A/B under the nearest existing lens, run on the re-baselined corpus, fails to recover them. No fifth lens is added from repeated false-positive anecdotes. The planned B/P/L/C comparison retains four lenses and preserves each lens's unique valid mechanisms, overlap, invalid/unresolved occurrences, misses and judge time separately from raw FAIL counts. L tests a conditional-rule bundle within existing scope. Seven unvalidated synthetic mechanism rows cannot establish the cross-source eligible-gap, triage-agreement or nearest-lens amendment conditions in this Target; the original historical triage limitations remain. All measurement is owner-paused; the verdict waits for the re-baseline (sc-2494).

Both tiers run over the same candidates and are fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (score = SUM of 1/(60+rank)), K=60 from Cormack et al. 2009 and deliberately untuned at this corpus size. Fusion matches or exceeds both tiers on every measured metric, and beats both only on multi-axis: containment SINGLE 8/8 (ties the semantic tier), Buried-by-rank 1/8, SetRecall 3/4 (vs 2/4 lexical and 1/4 semantic), PartialRecall 87.5% (vs 75% and 62.5%). That multi-axis family is 4 MULTI cases carrying 8 required-axis slots, so the three PartialRecall figures are 7/8, 6/8 and 5/8, and the whole result rests on one additional axis retrieved; the Wilson interval on SetRecall 3/4 is [30, 95], so the size of the win is not established at this corpus size. The tiers demonstrably fail on different cases, so fusion is preferred over laddering. Abstention, however, is computed from the PRE-FUSION lexical top-1 score, never the fused score: RRF is rank-only by construction and throws away the magnitude a confidence threshold needs. Degradation to a single tier is announced on stderr, and the result's source field reports hybrid, lexical or semantic so a caller can see which path ran.

Notes appended after a ruling are retrievable: each axis splits into entries, the current ruling block plus each note appended after it, every entry is scored independently, and the axis score is the MAX over its entries. A verdict-producing gate emits its INPUTS and its non-runs, not only its outcomes. (1) Every SELECTED reviewer emits review_scope BEFORE the judge runs — files, diff_sha256, file count and hash, and cached — so a cache hit is attributable on the same footing as a live run. (2) Every reviewer that did NOT run emits review_skipped with the reason (gate_disabled, no_llm, GUARD_REVIEW_SKIP, not_selected), so non-selection is a row and never an absence. (3) Every verdict carries prompt_identity: the same hash formula as the review-mode packaged preflight, computed over the assets the brief resolver picked (consumer override, else the running package) on the commit/ship path, so a production rate and a bench baseline are comparable when the bytes match. (4) The per-lens checklist vector rides on review_result INCLUDING the passes, with each failing lens attributed to what the gate did with it (blocking, waived, dropped_out_of_charter). Absent items means no artifact — a different fact from an artifact with zero failures.

During a commit, aggregate ratchets judge tracked state and require growth: compare the pending Git index with HEAD. Existing over-cap state at HEAD is reported as non-blocking drift with a baseline-refresh remedy; a clean-index CI or manual run still enforces the whole tree. Use direct index and tree readers rather than per-file staged scoping so merges remain aggregate-safe. Ratchet storage is ownership-based: guard-size and guard-fanout persist their engine-neutral size.json, size-lines.json, and fanout.json ceilings under .devkit/baselines, while eslint/baselines retains only the structure/import policy modules consumed by ESLint. Package-mode init/upgrade performs a one-way, byte-preserving migration that stages both sides of each tracked move, restoring narrowly scoped `.devkit/baselines` ignore exceptions before moving while preserving tracked manifests and standalone assets. Package-mode gate and freeze writes apply the same trackability preflight; overlay writes remain deliberately local; ship worktree baseline symlinks remain writable. The canonical addition is verified in Git before the legacy deletion is staged, so an interrupted index update preserves debt. Concurrent migrations and writers converge when either side completes the move first; equal duplicates collapse to the canonical copy, and differing live copies stop before any write. Until migration runs, mixed-version readers accept an existing legacy path and retry canonical after a disappearing legacy read; the next gate tightening or explicit freeze writes canonical state and removes both storage generations when debt clears. Ship/review projection and deterministic-prefix fingerprinting carry both directories. This changes storage, not the Target's staged/index attribution semantics.

A checklist-free reviewer's prose verdict never blocks by itself. Blocking authority requires the gate to mechanically parse at least one complete finding that satisfies the reviewer's declared evidence contract. A `FAIL` without such a finding is inconclusive, preserving strict ship's fail-closed boundary without misreporting a repository-rule violation. Under the conventions evidence contract (conventions-v3:grounded-quote), each OFFENDING quote must also be grounded before its pair keeps blocking authority: (1) the pair's path is in the reviewed set; (2) the normalized quote appears in the staged blob within ±3 lines of the cited line, or in a line the change removes (a +/- marked quote's body binds to that side of the diff, a literal staged line may itself start with -, and a +-marked quote never matches a removed line; a quote the judge wrapped across lines matches the smallest run of up to 4 joined lines); and (3) that line is part of this change: an added line, or any line of a file that grew versus HEAD (rename-aware). Grounding reads the staged tree and HEAD pinned when the judge evidence is cut, and grounds nothing whenever the index no longer holds that tree, rechecked on every grounding. Grounding runs before the path:line dedupe, and its lenses, keyed on the canonical path, are the only ones the override valve blocks on or waives. Same rule as dup-gate-evidence-verified-against-worktree; ratchets-blame-the-change-not-the-tree for size debt.

Retrieval candidates come from the decisions DIRECTORY (loadAxisRows in gate-engine/decisions/retrieval.mts), reading both the Target and the legacy pre-Target schema; INDEX.md is demoted to a rendered view that supplies ruling/why only as a fallback for a file we cannot parse. A searched-but-unmatched query ABSTAINS: RankResult.source distinguishes 'empty' (nothing recorded) from 'none' (searched, nothing rules) and returns no rows, replacing the alphabetical first-k fallback. A ruling is never served bare: an axis splits into ENTRIES, the current ruling block plus each note appended after it, every entry is scored independently, and the axis score is the MAX over its entries. Rows carry qualifiedBy; prose prints the 3 most query-relevant notes plus a count, and --json carries all. Qualifiers are ordered by their own relevance, not by date. A stale claim misleads only when served without its qualifiers, so staleness is judged structurally, not by supersession keywords.

Both tiers run over the same candidates and are fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (score = SUM of 1/(60+rank)), K=60 from Cormack et al. 2009 and deliberately untuned at this corpus size. Fusion ties the semantic tier on containment SINGLE (8/8 vs 8/8), has Buried-by-rank 1/8, and matches or exceeds both tiers on every measured metric, beating both only on the multi-axis family: SetRecall 3/4 (vs 2/4 lexical, 1/4 semantic) and PartialRecall 87.5% (vs 75% and 62.5%). That family is 4 MULTI cases carrying 8 required-axis slots, so the win rests on one additional axis retrieved, and its size is not established at this corpus size (Wilson interval on SetRecall 3/4 is [30, 95]). Fusing rather than laddering still holds, because the tiers fail on different cases. Abstention, however, is computed from the PRE-FUSION lexical top-1 score, never the fused score: RRF is rank-only by construction and throws away the magnitude a confidence threshold needs. Degradation to a single tier is announced on stderr, and the result's source field reports hybrid, lexical or semantic so a caller can see which path ran.

A verdict-producing gate emits its INPUTS and its non-runs, not only its outcomes. (1) Every SELECTED reviewer emits review_scope BEFORE the judge runs — files, diff_sha256, file count and hash, and cached — so a cache hit is attributable on the same footing as a live run. (2) Every reviewer that did NOT run emits review_skipped with the reason (gate_disabled, no_llm, GUARD_REVIEW_SKIP, not_selected), so non-selection is a row and never an absence. (3) Every verdict carries prompt_identity: the same hash formula as the review-mode packaged preflight, computed over the SYNCED consumer assets on the commit/ship path, so a production rate and a bench baseline are comparable when the bytes match. (4) The per-lens checklist vector rides on review_result INCLUDING the passes, with each failing lens attributed to what the gate did with it (blocking, waived, dropped_out_of_charter). Absent items means no artifact — a different fact from an artifact with zero failures. (5) A commit-guard PASS whose semantic retrieval did not run is marked, never reported as clean. The judge records retrieval as ok or unavailable with a cause in its checklist artifact (finalize --retrieval ok unavailable --cause), not in prose; the gate reads that record before the artifact is deleted and keeps status pass and the exit code (visible, not blocking, so an embeddings outage never fail-closes a ship). The degraded PASS is marked on every channel: the completion line reads PASS (DEGRADED), a ⚠️ advisory line is printed, a gate_degraded event is emitted (rendered by the ship digest as an unverified row via its optional detail field), review_result carries degraded_cause, and the cache entry stores degraded_cause so a replayed hit prints cached PASS (DEGRADED) and re-emits the event. An absent or malformed record degrades as 'not recorded', never assumed ok; a named skip is never degraded.

A registration whose command string changes records its prior spelling in SUPERSEDED_HOOK_COMMANDS, in SOURCE form, beside the live command. Reconciliation runs once per provider per destination before scope transfer, removal and install, and does two things in the same publishPlan transaction: it carries devkit's own ledger row forward onto the current spelling, and it strips the prior spelling from the provider document only at the event and matcher that ledger row names. Provider spellings are derived by running each table row through the same nativeProjection a live install uses, never hand-transcribed, so codex and cursor are covered by construction. The document strip is gated on a ledger row for that exact registration and owner holding either the prior or the current spelling; the second arm recovers the crash window inside publishPlan's ledger-document-ledger write order. The strip is confined to the event and matcher that row names, so a command string equal to the prior spelling under any other event or matcher is left untouched. This is distinct from RETIRED_COMMANDS, which handles a registration that is GONE and accepts the literal itself as ownership proof because a pre-ledger config has no row to vouch for it.

Split by ownership. (1) qavis owns the classifier (`route --staged|--diff --gate`, a haiku judge that reads the diff — bench-picked at recall 0.96 / false-advise 0.00, clearing the floors regex can't) and a content-addressed pass-receipt (`.qavis/receipt.json`, sha256 over each changed file's blob sha, so a staged index and an identical committed tree match). (2) devkit is a THIN CHANNEL: `gate-engine/qavis-advisory` shells `qavis route --staged --gate`, and fail-OPENS (exit 0) when qavis or a `.qavis/recipe.json` is absent — the fallow precedent, zero weight for non-qavis consumers. (3) The exit contract is advisory: 0 = continue (SILENT / advisory-only on a normal commit / receipt-cleared / qavis absent), 3 = ADVISE under a strict ship (`GUARD_AI_STRICT`) — the ship blocks until qavis runs (writing a receipt that clears it) or an override is set. There is NO exit 1 and NO fail-closed on outage (unlike completeness): an advisor's own failure must never block a ship. Overrides: `GUARD_QAVIS_OK=1` ships without QA, `GUARD_NO_QAVIS_ADVISORY=1` disables. Wired as its own husky fragment (bunx/standalone/overlay) with its own remedy line, NOT an AI_GUARD (different exit contract). On a devkit ship, every judge that can demand a source edit (guard-review, guard-sentry) runs before the qavis advisory, so a passing receipt is not voided by a later judge-forced fix; the advisory's ADVISE output states this order and names DEVKIT_SHIP_QA=1 as the in-run alternative, and never itself passes.

During a commit, aggregate ratchets judge tracked state and require growth: compare the pending Git index with HEAD. Existing over-cap state at HEAD is reported as non-blocking drift with a baseline-refresh remedy; a clean-index CI or manual run still enforces the whole tree. Use direct index and tree readers rather than per-file staged scoping so merges remain aggregate-safe. Ratchet storage is owned per engine: guard-size and guard-fanout persist size.json, size-lines.json, and fanout.json under .devkit/baselines, while eslint/baselines retains only the structure and import policy modules consumed by ESLint. A checklist-free reviewer's prose verdict never blocks by itself. Blocking authority requires the gate to mechanically parse at least one complete finding that satisfies the reviewer's declared evidence contract. A `FAIL` without such a finding is inconclusive, preserving strict ship's fail-closed boundary without misreporting a repository-rule violation. For the conventions evidence contract (identity conventions-v3:grounded-quote), a parsed OFFENDING pair keeps blocking authority only when all of these hold: (1) its path is in the reviewed set; (2) its normalized quote appears in the staged blob within ±3 lines of the cited line, or in a line the change removes (a +/- marked quote's body binds to that side of the diff, a literal staged line may itself start with -, and a +-marked quote never matches a removed line; a quote the judge wrapped across lines matches the smallest run of up to 4 joined lines); and (3) that line is part of this change: an added line, or any line of a file that grew versus HEAD (rename-aware). Grounding reads the staged tree and HEAD pinned when the judge evidence is cut, grounds nothing whenever the index no longer holds that tree (rechecked on every grounding), runs before the path:line dedupe, and its lenses, keyed on the canonical path, are the only ones the override valve blocks on or waives. Same rule as dup-gate-evidence-verified-against-worktree; ratchets-blame-the-change-not-the-tree for size debt.

Explicit paths remain the default for dirty-tree shipping. The opt-in --from-branch mode requires an explicit remote base, pins the base and current HEAD commits, proves ancestry, derives root-literal committed path membership, refuses in-scope overlays and unsupported path representations, and records branch source mode plus frozen membership for resume. Explicit ship and reship --pr path arguments are literal files resolved from the repo root, never pathspecs; each caller path reaches git as ':(literal)<path>' without 'top'. Ambient GIT_LITERAL/GLOB/NOGLOB/ICASE_PATHSPECS are unset in both modes, and reconcile-manifest-write classifies every path under --literal-pathspecs. Raw PATHS remains the storage and display identity, so receipts recorded before this change still resume. The directory refusal is framed on $ROOT like the git calls that consume the path.

The --fail gate evaluates, in order: hard floors on the safety metrics (DECISION recall / CONTRADICT precision / depth accuracy < 0.75 fail immediately), before any comparability early return including a comparability skip; then comparability preconditions (config + gate-code hash + corpus hash mismatches SKIP the flip comparison mechanically); then the per-row FLIP TABLE vs baseline judged by a mid-p McNemar test (p<0.05, ~5+ net one-directional flips) counting only STABLE flips (unanimous across BENCH_RUNS=3 majority-vote trials for detect/depth; retry-confirmed 2-of-2 for alignment). --fail with no baseline exits NON-ZERO ('cannot verify' is not 'verified fine'); compare's lines are printed even when no baseline file exists. Aggregate deltas print as informational only; every metric ships raw counts + a Wilson 95% interval plus an MDE line; every run appends to the runs.log ledger and post-fix rows enter as holdout.

devkit own test processes inherit NO run authority from whatever launched them. vitest.setup.mjs deletes an explicit, named list of ship/review authority variables before any test module loads (setupFiles runs per worker ahead of the first import, so even a top-level process.env capture sees the cleaned env), and both vitest configs share that one file. The scrubbed set is SCRUBBED_ENV, the union of three provenance lists: INHERITED_RUN_ENV, which mirrors the variables cli/lib/ship/review-target.sh unsets and is bound to it by a parity test (membership is reused, the reason is not: that script prevents inheriting a FOREIGN run authority); SHIP_EXPORTED_ENV, the variables ship-branch.sh and run-gates-with-capture.sh export beyond that set, some of which are read at runtime (DEVKIT_SHIP_ROOT and DEVKIT_SHIP_BRANCH change which repository and verdict a test sees); and TEST_ONLY_ADDITIONS, the FRINK_AI_STRICT alias. The binding test does not trust a hand-written list: it parses the export left-hand sides out of ship-branch.sh and run-gates-with-capture.sh and requires every DEVKIT_ or GUARD_ name found there to be scrubbed, so a new ship export is caught at the source. Deliberate invocation knobs are never scrubbed: SHIP_COMMIT_TIMEOUT and DEVKIT_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT are inputs a caller chose. A test that needs a policy var sets it explicitly. The guarantee is about INHERITANCE, not visibility - a per-worker setup file cannot undo a test that sets a var mid-file and never restores it.

Every completed row is appended to a gitignored progress-<sub>.jsonl the moment it lands, and re-running the SAME command replays those rows for free. A row is replayed only when config (model/K/cascade) AND gateHash AND corpusHash all match, so a stale checkpoint is inert rather than quietly blending two measurements; outage verdicts (NULL) are never replayed. If this bench ever gains an env-defined arm (a flag such as GUARD_CORRECTNESS_SPLIT that is not a source edit), its checkpoint filename must be keyed by that arm, as the review bench does with progress-<model>-<cascade>-split<sha8>.jsonl, because gateHash and corpusHash cannot see env flags and the replay predicate would otherwise blend one arm's rows into another's.

Only in-evidence-unmatched misses feed the lens question; attribution uses a pre-registered rubric (the four brief definitions plus an explicit none) whose light-judge triage must reach kappa >= 0.6 against hand labels before its column counts. A fifth lens is warranted only when a class no existing checklist names holds a clear majority of eligible misses (category denominator >= 8 catchable) across both sources AND a prompt-bullet A/B under the nearest existing lens, run on the re-baselined corpus, fails to recover them. No new category is added from repeated false-positive anecdotes. The planned B/P/L/C comparison retains four lenses and preserves each lens's unique valid mechanisms, overlap, invalid/unresolved occurrences, misses and judge time separately from raw FAIL counts. Seven unvalidated synthetic mechanism rows cannot establish the cross-source eligible-gap, triage-agreement or nearest-lens amendment conditions in this Target. All measurement is owner-paused; the verdict waits for the re-baseline (sc-2494).

Retrieval candidates come from the decisions DIRECTORY (loadAxisRows in gate-engine/decisions/retrieval.mts), reading both the Target and the legacy pre-Target schema; INDEX.md is demoted to a rendered view that supplies ruling/why only as a fallback for a file we cannot parse. A searched-but-unmatched query ABSTAINS: RankResult.source distinguishes 'empty' (nothing recorded) from 'none' (searched, nothing rules) and returns no rows, replacing the alphabetical first-k fallback. A ruling is never served bare: each axis splits into entries (the current ruling block plus each note appended after it), every entry is scored independently, and the axis score is the MAX over its entries. Rows carry qualifiedBy; prose prints the 3 most query-relevant notes plus a count, and --json carries all of them, ordered by their own relevance rather than date. A stale claim misleads only when served without its qualifiers.

Both tiers run over the same candidates and are fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (score = SUM of 1/(60+rank)), K=60 from Cormack et al. 2009 and deliberately untuned at this corpus size. Fusion matches or exceeds both tiers on every measured metric: containment SINGLE 8/8, Buried-by-rank 1/8, SetRecall 3/4, PartialRecall 87.5%. It beats BOTH parents only on the multi-axis family, and the size of that win is not established at this corpus size. Abstention, however, is computed from the PRE-FUSION lexical top-1 score, never the fused score: RRF is rank-only by construction and throws away the magnitude a confidence threshold needs. Degradation to a single tier is announced on stderr, and the result's source field reports hybrid, lexical or semantic so a caller can see which path ran.

A verdict-producing gate emits its INPUTS and its non-runs, not only its outcomes. (1) Every SELECTED reviewer emits review_scope BEFORE the judge runs — files, diff_sha256, file count and hash, and cached — so a cache hit is attributable on the same footing as a live run. (2) Every reviewer that did NOT run emits review_skipped with the reason (gate_disabled, no_llm, GUARD_REVIEW_SKIP, not_selected), so non-selection is a row and never an absence. (3) Every verdict carries prompt_identity: the same hash formula as the review-mode packaged preflight, computed over the SYNCED consumer assets on the commit/ship path, so a production rate and a bench baseline are comparable when the bytes match. (4) The per-lens checklist vector rides on review_result INCLUDING the passes, with each failing lens attributed to what the gate did with it (blocking, waived, dropped_out_of_charter). Absent items means no artifact — a different fact from an artifact with zero failures. (5) A PASS whose semantic retrieval did not run is marked DEGRADED, never assumed ok: the judge records its retrieval outcome in its checklist artifact via finalize --retrieval ok|unavailable --cause, never in prose; the gate reads that record before the artifact is deleted and keeps status pass and the exit code (visible, not blocking, so an embeddings outage never fail-closes a ship). A degraded pass is marked on every channel: the completion line reads PASS (DEGRADED), a ⚠️ advisory line is printed, a gate_degraded event is emitted (rendered by the ship digest as an unverified row via its optional detail field), degraded_cause is set on review_result and in the cache entry, so a replayed hit prints cached PASS (DEGRADED) and re-emits the event. An absent or malformed record degrades as 'not recorded'; a named skip is never degraded.

A registration whose command string changes records its prior spelling in SUPERSEDED_HOOK_COMMANDS, in SOURCE form, beside the live command. Reconciliation runs once per provider per destination before scope transfer, removal and install, and does two things in the same publishPlan transaction: it carries devkit's own ledger row forward onto the current spelling, and it strips the prior spelling from the provider document, only at the event and matcher that the ledger row names. Provider spellings are derived by running each table row through the same nativeProjection a live install uses, never hand-transcribed, so codex and cursor are covered by construction. The document strip is gated on a ledger row for that exact registration and owner holding either the prior or the current spelling, and it is keyed on that row's event and matcher as well as its command string, so a consumer command spelled the same but wired to another event or matcher is never removed. The second arm recovers the crash window inside publishPlan's ledger-document-ledger write order. The supersession strip and the RETIRED_COMMANDS removal share one stripHandlers walk taking an (event, matcher, command) predicate. This is distinct from RETIRED_COMMANDS, which handles a registration that is GONE and accepts the literal itself as ownership proof because a pre-ledger config has no row to vouch for it. A consumer who relocates devkit's command to another event keeps the relocated copy and gets a fresh canonical registration beside it.

A judge outage is CLASSIFIED at the failure site, not guessed at, and reachability is REPORTED before the chain but never enforced there. classifyJudgeOutage (gate-engine/judge/outage/classify.mts) splits absent / unauthenticated / rate-limited out of the fused offline/quota/absent label using only the provider's own channels — the structured turn.failed event and stderr, never the Node error message, which renders the judge's argv and therefore the staged diff. Every classification is positive-signal-only: an unrecognised failure stays transient. Each kind carries 'permanent', the single input to every retry predicate, replacing the cascade's firstOutage !== 'timeout' test. A ship-time preflight reads codex app-server account/rateLimits/read (non-billed, ~1s, answers while inference is refused) and prints provider, model, window use and reset per ROLE — then continues unconditionally.

Split by ownership. (1) qavis owns the classifier (`route --staged|--diff --gate`, a haiku judge that reads the diff — bench-picked at recall 0.96 / false-advise 0.00, clearing the floors regex can't) and a content-addressed pass-receipt (`.qavis/receipt.json`, sha256 over each changed file's blob sha, so a staged index and an identical committed tree match). (2) devkit is a THIN CHANNEL: `gate-engine/qavis-advisory` shells `qavis route --staged --gate`, and fail-OPENS (exit 0) when qavis or a `.qavis/recipe.json` is absent — the fallow precedent, zero weight for non-qavis consumers. On a devkit ship, every judge that can demand a source edit runs BEFORE the qavis advisory: pre-commit judges sentry ahead of the advisory when the ship message file is known (DEVKIT_COMMIT_MSG_FILE, excluding devkit review), and commit-msg replays that verdict from the diff-tier sentry cache, so a passing QA receipt is not voided by a later judge-forced fix. The ADVISE output under a ship states this order and names `DEVKIT_SHIP_QA=1` as the in-run alternative, suppressed when already set; the order is never a pass. Overlay installs no devkit commit-msg judge, so this ordering does not apply there. Non-diff sentry tiers (`GUARD_SENTRY_CONTEXT=message` names) are uncached and still re-judge at commit-msg. (3) The exit contract is advisory: 0 = continue (SILENT / advisory-only on a normal commit / receipt-cleared / qavis absent), 3 = ADVISE under a strict ship (`GUARD_AI_STRICT`) — the ship blocks until qavis runs (writing a receipt that clears it) or an override is set. There is NO exit 1 and NO fail-closed on outage (unlike completeness): an advisor's own failure must never block a ship. Overrides: `GUARD_QAVIS_OK=1` ships without QA, `GUARD_NO_QAVIS_ADVISORY=1` disables. Wired as its own husky fragment (bunx/standalone/overlay) with its own remedy line, NOT an AI_GUARD (different exit contract).

During a commit, aggregate ratchets judge tracked state and require growth: compare the pending Git index with HEAD. Existing over-cap state at HEAD is reported as non-blocking drift with a baseline-refresh remedy; a clean-index CI or manual run still enforces the whole tree. Use direct index and tree readers rather than per-file staged scoping so merges remain aggregate-safe. Ratchet storage is ownership-based: guard-size and guard-fanout persist their engine-neutral size.json, size-lines.json, and fanout.json ceilings under .devkit/baselines, while eslint/baselines retains only the structure/import policy modules consumed by ESLint. Package-mode init/upgrade performs a one-way, byte-preserving migration and stages both sides of each tracked move, restoring narrowly scoped `.devkit/baselines` ignore exceptions before moving while preserving tracked manifests and standalone assets. Package-mode gate/freeze writes apply the same trackability preflight; overlay writes remain deliberately local; ship worktree baseline symlinks remain writable. The canonical addition is verified in Git before the legacy deletion is staged, so an interrupted index update preserves debt. Concurrent migrations and writers converge when either side completes the move first. Equal duplicates collapse to the canonical copy; differing live copies stop before any write. Until migration runs, mixed-version readers accept an existing legacy path and retry canonical after a disappearing legacy read; the next gate tightening or explicit freeze writes canonical state and removes both storage generations when debt clears. Ship/review projection and deterministic-prefix fingerprinting carry both directories because both affect gate verdicts. This changes storage, not the Target’s staged/index attribution semantics.

A checklist-free reviewer's prose verdict never blocks by itself. Blocking authority requires the gate to mechanically parse at least one complete finding that satisfies the reviewer's declared evidence contract. A `FAIL` without such a finding is inconclusive, preserving strict ship's fail-closed boundary without misreporting a repository-rule violation. For the conventions contract (identity conventions-v3:grounded-quote), each OFFENDING pair keeps blocking authority only when (1) its path is in the reviewed set, (2) its normalized quote appears in the staged blob within ±3 lines of the cited line, or in a line the change removes (a +/- marked quote's body binds to that side of the diff, a literal staged line may itself start with -, a +-marked quote never matches a removed line, and a quote the judge wrapped across lines matches the smallest run of up to 4 joined lines), and (3) that line is part of this change: an added line, or any line of a file that grew versus HEAD (rename-aware). Grounding reads the staged tree and HEAD pinned when the judge evidence is cut, grounds nothing whenever the index no longer holds that tree (rechecked on every grounding), and runs before the path:line dedupe. Its lenses, keyed on the canonical path, are the only ones the override valve blocks on or waives.

Ship retries CONVERGE instead of restarting: (1) reviewer PASSes checkpoint per-completion, (2) an all-green deterministic prefix is cached on the staged tree hash (`guard-prefix`, armed only under `DEVKIT_SHIP=1` where worktree ≡ index), (3) decisions ROUTINE/ALIGN/depth-PASS verdicts are cached on their exact evidence bytes, (4) deterministic gate failures AGGREGATE into one report while AI gates stay fail-fast, and (5) under `GUARD_AI_STRICT=1` (exported only by ship) the reviewer gate's sonnet first pass retries once and an inconclusive-after-retry FAILS CLOSED with exit 3 — a code distinct from exit 1 so hooks never render an outage as an opus-confirmed FAIL; the decisions judges fail closed WITHOUT a retry (deliberate: retries there erode the ceiling for little value — alignment outage exits 3 named, detect's outage keeps its regex block standing but labels it UNVERIFIED with a remedy). A judge that times out is never re-run, so a stuck judge costs at most one cap.

Explicit paths remain the default for dirty-tree shipping. Explicit ship and reship --pr path arguments are literal files resolved from the repo root, never pathspecs: each caller path reaches git as ':(literal)<path>' without 'top', and ambient GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS, GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS, GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS and GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS are unset in both modes. Raw PATHS stays the storage and display identity, so receipts recorded before this rule still resume. Reconcile-manifest-write classifies every path under --literal-pathspecs, and both reconcile-manifest-write and devkit reconcile must scrub ambient pathspec modes through literalPathspecEnv(). The opt-in --from-branch mode requires an explicit remote base, pins the base and current HEAD commits, proves ancestry, derives root-literal committed path membership, refuses in-scope overlays and unsupported path representations, and records branch source mode plus frozen membership for resume.

devkit own test processes inherit NO run authority from whatever launched them. vitest.setup.mjs deletes an explicit, named list of ship/review authority variables before any test module loads (setupFiles runs per worker ahead of the first import, so even a top-level process.env capture sees the cleaned env), and both vitest configs share that one file. The scrub is three provenance lists: INHERITED_RUN_ENV, the vocabulary cli/lib/ship/review-target.sh unsets, bound to it by a parity test so the two can never drift; SHIP_EXPORTED_ENV, the DEVKIT_SHIP_* exports of ship-branch.sh and run-gates-with-capture.sh beyond that vocabulary; and TEST_ONLY_ADDITIONS, the FRINK_AI_STRICT alias. SCRUBBED_ENV is their union. Ship exports read at runtime are not inert: qavis-advisory shipMode() branches on DEVKIT_SHIP_ROOT, and review completeness verdictBranch() scopes a sticky verdict to DEVKIT_SHIP_BRANCH, so an inherited pair would make a test answer for the outer ship's repository. The binding test derives the ship exports by parsing the export left-hand sides out of ship-branch.sh and run-gates-with-capture.sh, and requires every DEVKIT_ or GUARD_ name found there to be scrubbed; it does not trust a hand-written list. Deliberate invocation knobs are never scrubbed: SHIP_COMMIT_TIMEOUT and DEVKIT_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT are inputs a caller chose. A test that needs a policy var sets it explicitly. The guarantee is about INHERITANCE, not visibility - a per-worker setup file cannot undo a test that sets a var mid-file and never restores it. vitest.e2e.config.mjs shares the same setupFiles, and a test asserts it.

The --fail gate evaluates, in order: hard floors on the safety metrics (DECISION recall / CONTRADICT precision / depth accuracy < 0.75 fail immediately), which are absolute properties of the current run and must precede every early return, including the no-baseline return and a comparability skip; then comparability preconditions (config + gate-code hash + corpus hash mismatches SKIP the comparison mechanically, never the floors); then the per-row FLIP TABLE vs baseline judged by a mid-p McNemar test (p<0.05, ~5+ net one-directional flips) counting only STABLE flips (unanimous across BENCH_RUNS=3 majority-vote trials for detect/depth; retry-confirmed 2-of-2 for alignment), which is the only step that requires a comparable baseline. --fail with no baseline exits non-zero ('cannot verify' is not 'verified fine'), and compare's lines are printed even when no baseline file exists. Aggregate deltas print as informational only; every metric ships raw counts + a Wilson 95% interval plus an MDE line; every run appends to the runs.log ledger and post-fix rows enter as holdout.

Row value is a COMPUTED property, printed by the harness, not assumed: a read-only audit (reviewers/audit.mts) reports never-measured, constant-correct, always-wrong and flipped rows, per-lens gold counts, pair groups (caseId ∪ variantOf, union-find) with an unmeasured member or straddling the holdout, unrelated near-twins (5-shingle Jaccard ≥ 0.5) and the holdout floor per class. Admission runs by coverage need, not supply: finalize --check refuses a proposal that is an unrelated near-twin of an existing row (an intended minimal pair — shared caseId or variantOf — is exempt) and prints the coverage cell the row fills. A FAIL row's defect must be introduced BY the diff and reachable from files in the fixture, and a PASS decoy must survive an adversarial read of its own note; both are check-list items for finalize --check reviewers. The 6 corpus-fault rows found by the 2026-09-03 always-wrong adjudication (docs/benchmarks/corpus-audit.md) are repaired inside the sc-2494 epoch break, not before it, so the corpus re-baselines once. Holdout is assigned per pair GROUP, never per row, and loadRows warns (DEVKIT_HOLDOUT_FLOOR_STRICT=1 refuses) when a class is under the floor. Pair-level contrast consistency is published beside the marginal; every reviewer ratio carries the measured label-noise floor (the Wilson upper bound, 13.9%, until a second κ round); mined candidates carry the label rule that minted them. Demotion of constant-correct rows to a tripwire tier happens ONLY on observations from the current epoch, after the re-baseline (sc-2494) — never on the sonnet/haiku 2026-08 checkpoints.

Every completed row is appended to a gitignored progress-<sub>.jsonl the moment it lands, and re-running the SAME command replays those rows for free. A row is replayed only when config (model/K/cascade) AND gateHash AND corpusHash all match, so a checkpoint made stale by a config, gate-source or corpus change is inert rather than quietly blending two measurements; outage verdicts (NULL) are never replayed. That predicate is blind to an arm defined by an env flag: a flag is not a source edit, so gateHash cannot see it and rows from one arm would be replayed into the other. An env-defined arm must therefore never share a checkpoint with another arm: either key the checkpoint FILENAME by arm, as the review bench does for its lens-split arm (progress-<model>-<cascade>-split<sha8>.jsonl), or add an arm dimension to the replay predicate. Cost and stability aggregates are derived from the ROWS (per-row inputChars/rawChars/judged/outage) rather than counters incremented in the loop, so a resumed run reports what the whole run cost. The reader drops torn trailing lines instead of failing the load. --fresh discards and re-measures.

Both tiers run over the same candidates and are fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (score = SUM of 1/(60+rank)), K=60 from Cormack et al. 2009 and deliberately untuned at this corpus size. Fusion matches or exceeds both tiers on every measured metric on the suite and beats both only on the multi-axis family: it TIES the semantic tier on Containment@5 SINGLE (8/8 vs 8/8), with Buried-by-rank 1/8, and wins outright on SetRecall (3/4 vs 2/4 lexical and 1/4 semantic) and PartialRecall (87.5% vs 75% and 62.5%, i.e. 7/8 vs 6/8 and 5/8). The size of that win is not established at this corpus size: the multi-axis family is 4 MULTI cases carrying 8 required-axis slots in total, so the whole result rests on ONE additional axis retrieved, and the Wilson interval on SetRecall 3/4 is [30, 95]. The tiers are fused rather than laddered because they demonstrably fail on different cases. Abstention, however, is computed from the PRE-FUSION lexical top-1 score, never the fused score: RRF is rank-only by construction and throws away the magnitude a confidence threshold needs. Degradation to a single tier is announced on stderr, and the result's source field reports hybrid, lexical or semantic so a caller can see which path ran.

A verdict-producing gate emits its INPUTS and its non-runs, not only its outcomes. (1) Every SELECTED reviewer emits review_scope BEFORE the judge runs — files, diff_sha256, file count and hash, and cached — so a cache hit is attributable on the same footing as a live run. (2) Every reviewer that did NOT run emits review_skipped with the reason (gate_disabled, no_llm, GUARD_REVIEW_SKIP, not_selected), so non-selection is a row and never an absence. (3) Every verdict carries prompt_identity: the same hash formula as the review-mode packaged preflight, computed over the SYNCED consumer assets on the commit/ship path, so a production rate and a bench baseline are comparable when the bytes match. (4) The per-lens checklist vector rides on review_result INCLUDING the passes, with each failing lens attributed to what the gate did with it (blocking, waived, dropped_out_of_charter). Absent items means no artifact — a different fact from an artifact with zero failures. (5) A commit-guard PASS whose semantic retrieval did not run is marked degraded and is never indistinguishable from a clean one: the judge records the retrieval outcome in its checklist artifact (finalize --retrieval ok|unavailable --cause), never in prose; the gate reads it before the artifact is deleted, keeps status pass and the exit code (visible, not blocking — an embeddings outage must not fail-close a ship), and marks it on every channel: the completion line reads PASS (DEGRADED), a ⚠️ advisory line, a gate_degraded event, degraded_cause on review_result, and degraded_cause in the cache entry so a replayed hit prints cached PASS (DEGRADED) and re-emits the event instead of a bare cached PASS. An absent or malformed retrieval record degrades as 'not recorded' and is never assumed ok; a named skip is never degraded.

A registration whose command string changes records its prior spelling in SUPERSEDED_HOOK_COMMANDS, in SOURCE form, beside the live command. Reconciliation runs once per provider per destination before scope transfer, removal and install, and does two things in the same publishPlan transaction: it carries devkit's own ledger row forward onto the current spelling, and it strips the prior spelling from the provider document. Provider spellings are derived by running each table row through the same nativeProjection a live install uses, never hand-transcribed, so codex and cursor are covered by construction. The document strip is gated on a ledger row for that exact registration and owner holding either the prior or the current spelling; the second arm recovers the crash window inside publishPlan's ledger-document-ledger write order. The strip only removes the prior spelling under the event and matcher that ledger row names, never wherever the command string appears: an identically spelled command under any other event or matcher group is consumer-owned and stays, including a copy of devkit's command a consumer relocated to another event, which is kept beside the fresh canonical registration. This is distinct from RETIRED_COMMANDS, which handles a registration that is GONE and accepts the literal itself as ownership proof because a pre-ledger config has no row to vouch for it. Retirement therefore matches the command string under any event, while supersession has a row and must stay inside it; both arms must go through the one shared stripHandlers walk and differ only in the (event, matcher, command) predicate they pass, never in a copied walk.

A judge outage is CLASSIFIED at the failure site, not guessed at, and reachability is REPORTED before the chain but never enforced there. classifyJudgeOutage (gate-engine/judge/outage/{classify,wording}.mts) splits absent / unauthenticated / rate-limited out of the fused offline/quota/absent label using only the provider's own channels — the structured turn.failed event and stderr, never the Node error message, which renders the judge's argv and therefore the staged diff. Every classification is positive-signal-only: an unrecognised failure stays transient. Each kind carries 'permanent', the single input to every retry predicate, replacing the cascade's firstOutage !== 'timeout' test. A ship-time preflight (cli/lib/ship/preflight/judge.mts) reads codex app-server account/rateLimits/read (non-billed, ~1s, answers while inference is refused) and prints provider, model, window use and reset per ROLE — then continues unconditionally.

Split by ownership. (1) qavis owns the classifier (`route --staged|--diff --gate`, a haiku judge that reads the diff — bench-picked at recall 0.96 / false-advise 0.00, clearing the floors regex can't) and a content-addressed pass-receipt (`.qavis/receipt.json`, sha256 over each changed file's blob sha, so a staged index and an identical committed tree match). (2) devkit is a THIN CHANNEL: `gate-engine/qavis-advisory` shells `qavis route --staged --gate`, and fail-OPENS (exit 0) when qavis or a `.qavis/recipe.json` is absent — the fallow precedent, zero weight for non-qavis consumers. (3) The exit contract is advisory: 0 = continue (SILENT / advisory-only on a normal commit / receipt-cleared / qavis absent), 3 = ADVISE under a strict ship (`GUARD_AI_STRICT`) — the ship blocks until qavis runs (writing a receipt that clears it) or an override is set. There is NO exit 1 and NO fail-closed on outage (unlike completeness): an advisor's own failure must never block a ship. Overrides: `GUARD_QAVIS_OK=1` ships without QA, `GUARD_NO_QAVIS_ADVISORY=1` disables. Wired as its own husky fragment (bunx/standalone/overlay) with its own remedy line, NOT an AI_GUARD (different exit contract). (4) Order on a devkit ship: every judge that can demand a source edit must run BEFORE the advisory, so a passing QA receipt is not voided by a later judge-forced fix — the advisory stays in pre-commit, and when the ship message file is known (`DEVKIT_COMMIT_MSG_FILE`, excluding `devkit review`) pre-commit judges guard-sentry ahead of the advisory (package + standalone builders) and commit-msg replays that verdict from the diff-tier sentry cache instead of re-voting. The ADVISE output under ship states that order (order only, never a pass: fail-open reviewers and `GUARD_NO_REVIEW` also reach it) and names `DEVKIT_SHIP_QA=1` as the in-run alternative, suppressed when already set. The overlay fragment is deliberately left without this ordering (it installs no devkit commit-msg judge, so none follows its advisory), and the non-diff sentry tiers (`GUARD_SENTRY_CONTEXT=message`) are uncached by design and still re-judge at commit-msg.

During a commit, aggregate ratchets judge tracked state and require growth: compare the pending Git index with HEAD. Existing over-cap state at HEAD is reported as non-blocking drift with a baseline-refresh remedy; a clean-index CI or manual run still enforces the whole tree. Use direct index and tree readers rather than per-file staged scoping so merges remain aggregate-safe. Ratchet storage is ownership-based: guard-size and guard-fanout persist their engine-neutral size.json, size-lines.json, and fanout.json ceilings only under .devkit/baselines, while eslint/baselines retains only the structure/import policy modules consumed by ESLint. Migration from the legacy location is one-way and byte-preserving: the canonical addition must be verified in Git before the legacy deletion is staged, equal duplicates collapse to the canonical copy, and differing live copies stop before any write. Until migration runs, readers must accept an existing legacy path and retry canonical after a disappearing legacy read. Ship/review projection and deterministic-prefix fingerprinting must carry both directories because both affect gate verdicts.

A checklist-free reviewer's prose verdict never blocks by itself. Blocking authority requires the gate to mechanically parse at least one complete finding that satisfies the reviewer's declared evidence contract. A `FAIL` without such a finding is inconclusive, preserving strict ship's fail-closed boundary without misreporting a repository-rule violation. Under the conventions evidence contract (identity `conventions-v3:grounded-quote`), parsing an OFFENDING quote is not enough: each path/quote pair must also be grounded, and a pair keeps blocking authority only when (1) its path is in the reviewed set, (2) the normalized quote appears in the staged blob within ±3 lines of the cited line, or in a line the change removes (a +/- marked quote's body binds to that side of the diff, a literal staged line may itself start with -, a +-marked quote never matches a removed line, and a quote the judge wrapped across lines matches the smallest run of up to 4 joined lines), and (3) that line is part of this change: an added line, or any line of a file that grew versus HEAD (rename-aware). Grounding reads the staged tree and HEAD pinned when the judge evidence is cut, grounds nothing whenever the index no longer holds that tree (rechecked on every grounding), and runs before the path:line dedupe. Grounding's lenses, keyed on the canonical path, are the only ones the override valve blocks on or waives.

devkit own test processes inherit NO run authority from whatever launched them. vitest.setup.mjs deletes an explicit, named list of ship/review authority variables before any test module loads (setupFiles runs per worker ahead of the first import, so even a top-level process.env capture sees the cleaned env), and both vitest configs share that one file. The list, SCRUBBED_ENV, is the union of three provenance lists: INHERITED_RUN_ENV, the vocabulary cli/lib/ship/review-target.sh unsets, bound to it by a parity test so the two can never drift (membership is reused, the reason is not: that script prevents inheriting a FOREIGN run authority at a review entrypoint, so its list is not a superset of what a ship exports); SHIP_EXPORTED_ENV, the variables ship-branch.sh exports beyond that vocabulary (DEVKIT_SHIP_BRANCH, DEVKIT_SHIP_DRY_GATES, DEVKIT_SHIP_FROM_BRANCH, DEVKIT_SHIP_INTENT_RECORDED, DEVKIT_SHIP_PATHS, DEVKIT_SHIP_REPO, DEVKIT_SHIP_RESUMED, DEVKIT_SHIP_ROOT); and TEST_ONLY_ADDITIONS (the FRINK_AI_STRICT alias). A binding test parses the export left-hand sides out of ship-branch.sh and run-gates-with-capture.sh and requires every DEVKIT_/GUARD_ name found there to be in SCRUBBED_ENV, so a new ship export must be added to the scrub at the source, never left to a hand-written list. A test also asserts that vitest.e2e.config.mjs uses the same setupFiles. Deliberate invocation knobs are never scrubbed: SHIP_COMMIT_TIMEOUT and DEVKIT_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT are inputs a caller chose. A test that needs a policy var sets it explicitly. The guarantee is about INHERITANCE, not visibility - a per-worker setup file cannot undo a test that sets a var mid-file and never restores it.

The --fail gate evaluates, in order: hard floors on the safety metrics (DECISION recall / CONTRADICT precision / depth accuracy < 0.75 fail immediately), comparability preconditions (config + gate-code hash + corpus hash mismatches SKIP the comparison mechanically), then the per-row FLIP TABLE vs baseline judged by a mid-p McNemar test (p<0.05, ~5+ net one-directional flips) counting only STABLE flips (unanimous across BENCH_RUNS=3 majority-vote trials for detect/depth; retry-confirmed 2-of-2 for alignment). A floor is absolute (a property of this run, needing no baseline), so the floor check must precede every early return, including the no-baseline return and a comparability skip; only the flip table requires a comparable baseline. --fail with no baseline exits non-zero ('cannot verify' is not 'verified fine'), and compare's lines are always printed, even when no baseline file exists. Aggregate deltas print as informational only; every metric ships raw counts + a Wilson 95% interval plus an MDE line; every run appends to the runs.log ledger and post-fix rows enter as holdout.

Every completed row is appended to a gitignored progress-<sub>.jsonl the moment it lands, and re-running the SAME command replays those rows for free. A row is replayed only when config (model/K/cascade) AND gateHash AND corpusHash all match, so a stale checkpoint is inert rather than quietly blending two measurements; outage verdicts (NULL) are never replayed. That predicate cannot see an arm defined by an env flag, because a flag is not a source edit and leaves gateHash unchanged, so if this bench ever gains an env-defined arm, each arm must get its own checkpoint file keyed by arm in the filename, as the review bench does with progress-<model>-<cascade>-split<sha8>.jsonl, or the predicate must grow an arm dimension, so that one arm's rows are never replayed into another. Cost and stability aggregates are derived from the ROWS (per-row inputChars/rawChars/judged/outage) rather than counters incremented in the loop, so a resumed run reports what the whole run cost. The reader drops torn trailing lines instead of failing the load. --fresh discards and re-measures.

Row value is a COMPUTED property, printed by the harness, not assumed: a read-only audit (reviewers/audit.mts) reports never-measured, constant-correct, always-wrong and flipped rows, per-lens gold counts, pair groups (caseId ∪ variantOf, union-find) with an unmeasured member or straddling the holdout, unrelated near-twins (5-shingle Jaccard ≥ 0.5) and the holdout floor per class. Admission runs by coverage need, not supply: finalize --check refuses a proposal that is an unrelated near-twin of an existing row (an intended minimal pair — shared caseId or variantOf — is exempt) and prints the coverage cell the row fills. A FAIL row's defect must be introduced BY the diff and reachable from files in the fixture, and a PASS decoy must survive an adversarial read of its own note; both are check-list items for finalize --check reviewers. Holdout is assigned per pair GROUP, never per row, and loadRows warns (DEVKIT_HOLDOUT_FLOOR_STRICT=1 refuses) when a class is under the floor. Pair-level contrast consistency is published beside the marginal; every reviewer ratio carries the measured label-noise floor (the Wilson upper bound, 13.9%, until a second κ round); mined candidates carry the label rule that minted them. Demotion of constant-correct rows to a tripwire tier happens ONLY on observations from the current epoch, after the re-baseline (sc-2494) — never on the sonnet/haiku 2026-08 checkpoints. The 6 corpus-fault rows adjudicated in the always-wrong bucket (docs/benchmarks/corpus-audit.md) are repaired inside the sc-2494 epoch break, never before it, so the corpus re-baselines once.

Markdown structure is read by mdast-util-from-markdown in one module (gate-engine/decisions/recall/markdown.mts), which is the only place permitted to know markdown layout. A section is 'this heading until the next heading', read off parser node offsets rather than inferred, so a boundary cannot be half-right. Retrieval consumes sections(); sliceToNextHeading, upToFirstNote and every lastIndexOf offset walk are deleted. Frontmatter stays hand-rolled — it parses exactly the two documented fields.

Lens holes are MEASURED before any lens is added, with one reusable reducer (external/holes.mts): a second detector's labelled findings are joined to what the correctness reviewer held in scope, saw in full, and said on the same change, and every miss is partitioned not-reviewed / not-in-scope / evidence-uncertain / in-evidence-unmatched / matched BEFORE any lens attribution. Only in-evidence-unmatched misses feed the lens question; attribution uses a pre-registered rubric (the four brief definitions plus an explicit none) whose light-judge triage must reach kappa >= 0.6 against hand labels before its column counts. A fifth lens is warranted only when a class no existing checklist names holds a clear majority of eligible misses (category denominator >= 8 catchable) across both sources AND a prompt-bullet A/B under the nearest existing lens, run on the re-baselined corpus, fails to recover them. No new category is added from repeated false-positive anecdotes, and unvalidated synthetic mechanism rows cannot establish the cross-source eligible-gap, triage-agreement or nearest-lens conditions. The sc-2872 v2 B/P/L/C comparison retains four lenses and keeps each lens's unique valid mechanisms, overlap, invalid/unresolved occurrences, misses and judge time separate from raw FAIL counts; L tests a conditional-rule bundle within existing scope. All measurement is owner-paused; the verdict waits for the re-baseline (sc-2494).

A verdict-producing gate emits its INPUTS and its non-runs, not only its outcomes. (1) Every SELECTED reviewer emits review_scope BEFORE the judge runs — files, diff_sha256, file count and hash, and cached — so a cache hit is attributable on the same footing as a live run. (2) Every reviewer that did NOT run emits review_skipped with the reason (gate_disabled, no_llm, GUARD_REVIEW_SKIP, not_selected), so non-selection is a row and never an absence. (3) Every verdict carries prompt_identity: the same hash formula as the review-mode packaged preflight, computed over the SYNCED consumer assets on the commit/ship path, so a production rate and a bench baseline are comparable when the bytes match. (4) The per-lens checklist vector rides on review_result INCLUDING the passes, with each failing lens attributed to what the gate did with it (blocking, waived, dropped_out_of_charter). Absent items means no artifact — a different fact from an artifact with zero failures. (5) A commit-guard PASS whose semantic retrieval did not run is never emitted as a bare PASS: the judge records the retrieval outcome in its checklist artifact (finalize --retrieval, ok or unavailable with --cause), never in prose, and the gate reads it before the artifact is deleted, keeps status pass and the exit code (visible, not blocking — an embeddings outage must not fail-close a ship), and marks it on every channel: the completion line reads PASS (DEGRADED), a ⚠️ advisory line, a gate_degraded event, degraded_cause on review_result, and degraded_cause in the cache entry so a replayed hit prints cached PASS (DEGRADED) and re-emits the event. An absent or malformed retrieval record degrades as 'not recorded' and is never assumed ok; a named skip is never degraded.

A registration whose command string changes records every prior spelling it has shipped in SUPERSEDED_HOOK_COMMANDS, in SOURCE form, beside the live command, one table row per prior spelling; a registration can have more than one, and those rows share a single current command. Reconciliation runs once per provider per destination before scope transfer, removal and install, and does two things in the same publishPlan transaction: it carries devkit's own ledger row forward onto the current spelling, and it strips every prior spelling of that registration from the provider document. Provider spellings are derived by running each table row through the same nativeProjection a live install uses, never hand-transcribed, so codex and cursor are covered by construction. The document strip is gated on a ledger row for that exact registration and owner holding either any one of the prior spellings or the current spelling; the second arm recovers the crash window inside publishPlan's ledger-document-ledger write order. A claimed row authorises stripping EVERY prior spelling of that registration at the location the row names, not just the spelling the row itself holds, and never only the first table row that matches: a row carrying the current command carries no information about which prior spelling the document still has, and devkit is the sole writer of those strings. This is distinct from RETIRED_COMMANDS, which handles a registration that is GONE and accepts the literal itself as ownership proof because a pre-ledger config has no row to vouch for it.

During a commit, aggregate ratchets judge tracked state and require growth: compare the pending Git index with HEAD. Existing over-cap state at HEAD is reported as non-blocking drift with a baseline-refresh remedy; a clean-index CI or manual run still enforces the whole tree. Use direct index and tree readers rather than per-file staged scoping so merges remain aggregate-safe. Ratchet storage is ownership-based: guard-size and guard-fanout persist their size.json, size-lines.json, and fanout.json ceilings under .devkit/baselines, and eslint/baselines holds only the structure/import policy modules consumed by ESLint. Migration from the legacy location is one-way and byte-preserving: verify the canonical addition in Git before staging the legacy deletion, collapse equal duplicates to the canonical copy, and stop before any write when live copies differ. Split by ownership. (1) qavis owns the classifier (`route --staged|--diff --gate`, a haiku judge that reads the diff — bench-picked at recall 0.96 / false-advise 0.00, clearing the floors regex can't) and a content-addressed pass-receipt (`.qavis/receipt.json`, sha256 over each changed file's blob sha, so a staged index and an identical committed tree match). (2) devkit is a THIN CHANNEL: `gate-engine/qavis-advisory` shells `qavis route --staged --gate`, and fail-OPENS (exit 0) when qavis or a `.qavis/recipe.json` is absent — the fallow precedent, zero weight for non-qavis consumers. There is NO exit 1 and NO fail-closed on outage (unlike completeness): an advisor's own failure must never block a ship. Overrides: `GUARD_QAVIS_OK=1` ships without QA, `GUARD_NO_QAVIS_ADVISORY=1` disables. Overlay is exempt from the ordering: it installs no devkit commit-msg judge. The non-diff sentry tiers are uncached by design and still re-judge at commit-msg.

A checklist-free reviewer's prose verdict never blocks by itself. Blocking authority requires the gate to mechanically parse at least one complete finding that satisfies the reviewer's declared evidence contract. Under the conventions evidence contract (identity `conventions-v3:grounded-quote`) parsing alone is not enough: each OFFENDING quote must be grounded, and a pair keeps blocking authority only when (1) its path is in the reviewed set, (2) the normalized quote appears in the staged blob within ±3 lines of the cited line, or in a line the change removes, and (3) that line is part of this change: an added line, or any line of a file that grew versus HEAD (rename-aware). A +/- marked quote's body binds to that side of the diff, a literal staged line may itself start with -, a +-marked quote never matches a removed line, and a quote the judge wrapped across lines matches the smallest run of up to 4 joined lines. Grounding reads the staged tree and HEAD pinned when the judge evidence is cut, grounds nothing whenever the index no longer holds that tree (rechecked on every grounding), and runs before the path:line dedupe. Its lenses, keyed on the canonical path, are the only ones the override valve blocks on or waives.

devkit own test processes inherit NO run authority from whatever launched them. vitest.setup.mjs deletes an explicit, named list of ship/review authority variables before any test module loads (setupFiles runs per worker ahead of the first import, so even a top-level process.env capture sees the cleaned env), and both vitest configs share that one file. A binding test parses the export left-hand sides out of ship-branch.sh and run-gates-with-capture.sh and requires every DEVKIT_/GUARD_ name found there to be scrubbed, so a future ship export is caught at the source and must be added to the scrub. A test also asserts that vitest.e2e.config.mjs shares the same setupFiles. Deliberate invocation knobs are never scrubbed: SHIP_COMMIT_TIMEOUT and DEVKIT_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT are inputs a caller chose. A test that needs a policy var sets it explicitly. The guarantee is about INHERITANCE, not visibility - a per-worker setup file cannot undo a test that sets a var mid-file and never restores it.

The --fail gate evaluates, in order: hard floors on the safety metrics (DECISION recall / CONTRADICT precision / depth accuracy < 0.75 fail immediately), then comparability preconditions (config + gate-code hash + corpus hash mismatches SKIP the comparison mechanically), then the per-row FLIP TABLE vs baseline judged by a mid-p McNemar test (p<0.05, ~5+ net one-directional flips) counting only STABLE flips (unanimous across BENCH_RUNS=3 majority-vote trials for detect/depth; retry-confirmed 2-of-2 for alignment). The hard floors are absolute (a property of this run, needing no baseline), so they must be evaluated before every early return, including the no-baseline return and a comparability skip; only the flip table requires a comparable baseline. --fail with no baseline exits non-zero ('cannot verify' is not 'verified fine'), and compare's lines are always printed, even when no baseline file exists. Aggregate deltas print as informational only; every metric ships raw counts + a Wilson 95% interval plus an MDE line; every run appends to the runs.log ledger and post-fix rows enter as holdout.

Every completed row is appended to a gitignored progress-<sub>.jsonl the moment it lands, and re-running the SAME command replays those rows for free. A row is replayed only when config (model/K/cascade) AND gateHash AND corpusHash all match, so a stale checkpoint is inert rather than quietly blending two measurements; outage verdicts (NULL) are never replayed. That predicate is blind to env-flag arms, because an env flag is not a source edit and gateHash cannot see it; if this bench ever gains an env-defined arm, its checkpoint must be partitioned by arm, either by keying the checkpoint filename by arm as the review bench does (progress-<model>-<cascade>-split<sha8>.jsonl) or by adding an arm dimension to the replay predicate, so that one arm's rows are never replayed into another. Cost and stability aggregates are derived from the ROWS (per-row inputChars/rawChars/judged/outage) rather than counters incremented in the loop, so a resumed run reports what the whole run cost. The reader drops torn trailing lines instead of failing the load. --fresh discards and re-measures.

Row value is a COMPUTED property, printed by the harness, not assumed: a read-only audit (reviewers/audit.mts) reports never-measured, constant-correct, always-wrong and flipped rows, per-lens gold counts, pair groups (caseId ∪ variantOf, union-find) with an unmeasured member or straddling the holdout, unrelated near-twins (5-shingle Jaccard ≥ 0.5) and the holdout floor per class. Admission runs by coverage need, not supply: finalize --check refuses a proposal that is an unrelated near-twin of an existing row (an intended minimal pair — shared caseId or variantOf — is exempt) and prints the coverage cell the row fills. A FAIL row's defect must be introduced BY the diff and reachable from files in the fixture, and a PASS decoy must survive an adversarial read of its own note; both are check-list items for finalize --check reviewers. Holdout is assigned per pair GROUP, never per row, and loadRows warns (DEVKIT_HOLDOUT_FLOOR_STRICT=1 refuses) when a class is under the floor. Pair-level contrast consistency is published beside the marginal; every reviewer ratio carries the measured label-noise floor (the Wilson upper bound, 13.9%, until a second κ round); mined candidates carry the label rule that minted them. Demotion of constant-correct rows to a tripwire tier happens ONLY on observations from the current epoch, after the re-baseline (sc-2494) — never on the sonnet/haiku 2026-08 checkpoints. The 6 always-wrong rows adjudicated as corpus faults on 2026-09-03 (docs/benchmarks/corpus-audit.md) are repaired inside the sc-2494 epoch break, never before it, so the corpus re-baselines once.

Markdown structure is read by mdast-util-from-markdown in one module (gate-engine/decisions/recall/markdown.mts), which is the only place permitted to know markdown layout. A section is 'this heading until the next heading', read off parser node offsets rather than inferred, so a boundary cannot be half-right. Retrieval consumes sections(); sliceToNextHeading, upToFirstNote and every lastIndexOf offset walk are deleted. Frontmatter stays hand-rolled — it parses exactly the two documented fields.

Lens holes are MEASURED before any lens is added, with one reusable reducer (external/holes.mts): a second detector's labelled findings are joined to what the correctness reviewer held in scope, saw in full, and said on the same change, and every miss is partitioned not-reviewed / not-in-scope / evidence-uncertain / in-evidence-unmatched / matched BEFORE any lens attribution. CodeRabbit categories on devkit's own repos are the primary instrument ($0, 100% marker parse, verification-trace roots dropped); Martian Code Review Bench goldens are a confirmatory external precision/recall probe and a source of miss candidates only. Only in-evidence-unmatched misses feed the lens question; attribution uses a pre-registered rubric (the four brief definitions plus an explicit none) whose light-judge triage must reach kappa >= 0.6 against hand labels before its column counts. A fifth lens is warranted only when a class no existing checklist names holds a clear majority of eligible misses (category denominator >= 8 catchable) across both sources AND a prompt-bullet A/B under the nearest existing lens, run on the re-baselined corpus, fails to recover them. All measurement is owner-paused; the verdict waits for the re-baseline (sc-2494).

Retrieval candidates come from the decisions DIRECTORY (loadAxisRows in gate-engine/decisions/retrieval.mts), reading both the Target and the legacy pre-Target schema; INDEX.md is demoted to a rendered view that supplies ruling/why only as a fallback for a file we cannot parse. A searched-but-unmatched query ABSTAINS: RankResult.source distinguishes 'empty' (nothing recorded) from 'none' (searched, nothing rules) and returns no rows, replacing the alphabetical first-k fallback. Notes are retrievable: an axis splits into ENTRIES — the current ruling block plus each note appended after it — every entry is scored independently, and the axis score is the MAX over its entries, never a concatenation (clampGist is tail-biased, so note churn would outrank the ruling) and never a sum (note count must not be a ranking advantage). A ruling is never served bare: rows carry qualifiedBy, ordered by each note's OWN query relevance, not date; prose prints the 3 most query-relevant notes plus a count, and --json carries all.

Both tiers run over the same candidates and are fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (score = SUM of 1/(60+rank)), K=60 from Cormack et al. 2009 and deliberately untuned at this corpus size. Fusion matches or exceeds both tiers on every measured metric on the suite and beats both only on the multi-axis family: containment SINGLE 8/8 (a tie with the semantic tier's 8/8), Buried-by-rank 1/8, SetRecall 3/4 (vs 2/4 lexical and 1/4 semantic), PartialRecall 87.5% (7/8 required-axis slots, vs 6/8 lexical and 5/8 semantic). The size of that win is not established at this corpus size: the multi-axis family is 4 MULTI cases carrying 8 required-axis slots in total, so the result rests on ONE additional axis retrieved, and the Wilson interval on SetRecall 3/4 is [30, 95]. The tiers are fused rather than laddered because they demonstrably fail on different cases. Abstention, however, is computed from the PRE-FUSION lexical top-1 score, never the fused score: RRF is rank-only by construction and throws away the magnitude a confidence threshold needs. Degradation to a single tier is announced on stderr, and the result's source field reports hybrid, lexical or semantic so a caller can see which path ran.

The document strip is gated on a ledger row for that exact registration and owner holding either the prior or the current spelling; the second arm recovers the crash window inside publishPlan's ledger-document-ledger write order. The strip is confined to the event and matcher that ledger row names, never keyed on the command string alone: an identically spelled command under any other event or matcher group is consumer-owned and is left in place, per non-devkit-asset-collision-preserve. This is distinct from RETIRED_COMMANDS, which handles a registration that is GONE and accepts the literal itself as ownership proof because a pre-ledger config has no row to vouch for it. That asymmetry is deliberate: retirement matches the literal wherever it appears, while supersession has a row naming where devkit put the command and must stay inside it. Both arms share one stripHandlers walk taking an (event, matcher, command) predicate and differ only in that predicate, never in a copied walk. A consumer who relocates devkit's command to another event keeps the relocated copy and gets a fresh canonical registration beside it.

A registration whose command string changes records every prior spelling in SUPERSEDED_HOOK_COMMANDS, in SOURCE form, beside the live command, one row per spelling, so a registration that has shipped more than one prior spelling has several rows sharing a single current command.
