Every Devkit-spawned claude -p judge uses Claude Code strict MCP configuration. Pure and internal judges receive an empty profile. Named reviewer agents receive trusted machine-local codebase, Context7, and autonomous_bugs definitions when configured, and the full autonomous_bugs server permission includes report and amend. Definitions come only from user-owned Claude configuration or an explicit machine-local override, never repository-controlled .mcp.json. Task-dispatched agents use provider-native named server references and retain role-specific research capabilities. Claude agent assets must declare their MCP servers as native mcpServers list frontmatter so the references survive Devkit projection and installation. Secret-bearing definitions travel through private temporary files, not process arguments.

A judge outage is CLASSIFIED at the failure site, not guessed at, and reachability is REPORTED before the chain but never enforced there. classifyJudgeOutage (gate-engine/judge/outage/{classify,wording}.mts) splits absent / unauthenticated / rate-limited out of the fused offline/quota/absent label using only the provider's own channels — the structured turn.failed event and stderr, never the Node error message, which renders the judge's argv and therefore the staged diff. Every classification is positive-signal-only: an unrecognised failure stays transient. Each kind carries 'permanent', the single input to every retry predicate, replacing the cascade's firstOutage !== 'timeout' test. A ship-time preflight reads codex app-server account/rateLimits/read (non-billed, ~1s, answers while inference is refused) and prints provider, model, window use and reset per ROLE — then continues unconditionally.

During a commit, aggregate ratchets judge tracked state and require growth: compare the pending Git index with HEAD. Existing over-cap state at HEAD is reported as non-blocking drift with a baseline-refresh remedy; a clean-index CI or manual run still enforces the whole tree. Use direct index and tree readers rather than per-file staged scoping so merges remain aggregate-safe. Ratchet storage is ownership-based: guard-size and guard-fanout ceilings (size.json, size-lines.json, fanout.json) must live under .devkit/baselines, and eslint/baselines holds only the structure/import policy modules consumed by ESLint. Writers must write only the canonical .devkit/baselines copy, verify the canonical addition in Git before staging the legacy deletion, collapse equal duplicates to the canonical copy, and stop before any write when live copies differ. Until migration runs, readers must accept an existing legacy path and retry canonical after a disappearing legacy read. Ship/review projection and deterministic-prefix fingerprinting must carry both directories.

Split by ownership. (1) qavis owns the classifier (`route --staged|--diff --gate`, a haiku judge that reads the diff — bench-picked at recall 0.96 / false-advise 0.00, clearing the floors regex can't) and a content-addressed pass-receipt (`.qavis/receipt.json`, sha256 over each changed file's blob sha, so a staged index and an identical committed tree match). (2) devkit is a THIN CHANNEL: `gate-engine/qavis-advisory` shells `qavis route --staged --gate`, and fail-OPENS (exit 0) when qavis or a `.qavis/recipe.json` is absent — the fallow precedent, zero weight for non-qavis consumers. (3) The exit contract is advisory: 0 = continue (SILENT / advisory-only on a normal commit / receipt-cleared / qavis absent), 3 = ADVISE under a strict ship (`GUARD_AI_STRICT`) — the ship blocks until qavis runs (writing a receipt that clears it) or an override is set. There is NO exit 1 and NO fail-closed on outage (unlike completeness): an advisor's own failure must never block a ship. Overrides: `GUARD_QAVIS_OK=1` ships without QA, `GUARD_NO_QAVIS_ADVISORY=1` disables. Wired as its own husky fragment (bunx/standalone/overlay) with its own remedy line, NOT an AI_GUARD (different exit contract). (4) Order on a devkit ship: every judge that can demand a source edit runs BEFORE the advisory, so a passing receipt is never voided by a later judge-forced fix. guard-review exits 1 ahead of it at pre-commit; when the ship message file is known (`DEVKIT_COMMIT_MSG_FILE`, excluding devkit review), pre-commit also judges guard-sentry ahead of the advisory (package + standalone builders; overlay installs no commit-msg judge, so is unwired) and commit-msg replays that verdict from the diff-tier sentry cache; non-diff sentry tiers (`GUARD_SENTRY_CONTEXT=message`) are uncached and still re-judge at commit-msg. The advisory stays in pre-commit, never commit-msg. ADVISE output under ship states the order only, never a pass, and names `DEVKIT_SHIP_QA=1` as the in-run alternative.

A checklist-free reviewer's prose verdict never blocks by itself. Blocking authority requires the gate to mechanically parse at least one complete finding that satisfies the reviewer's declared evidence contract. A `FAIL` without such a finding is inconclusive, preserving strict ship's fail-closed boundary without misreporting a repository-rule violation. The conventions evidence contract (identity conventions-v3:grounded-quote) must ground each OFFENDING quote, not only parse it: a pair keeps blocking authority only when (1) its path is in the reviewed set, (2) the normalized quote appears in the staged blob within ±3 lines of the cited line, or in a line the change removes, and (3) that line is part of this change: an added line, or any line of a file that grew versus HEAD (rename-aware). In quote matching, a +/- marked quote's body binds to that side of the diff, a literal staged line may itself start with -, a +-marked quote never matches a removed line, and a quote the judge wrapped across lines matches the smallest run of up to 4 joined lines. Grounding reads the staged tree and HEAD pinned when the judge evidence is cut, and grounds nothing whenever the index no longer holds that tree, rechecked on every grounding. Grounding runs before the path:line dedupe, and the grounded lenses, keyed on the canonical path, are the only ones the override valve blocks on or waives.

Explicit paths remain the default for dirty-tree shipping. The opt-in --from-branch mode requires an explicit remote base, pins the base and current HEAD commits, proves ancestry, derives root-literal committed path membership, refuses in-scope overlays and unsupported path representations, and records branch source mode plus frozen membership for resume. Explicit ship and reship --pr path arguments are literal files resolved from the repo root, never pathspecs, and there is no opt-in flag for arbitrary pathspecs. Each caller path must reach git as ':(literal)<path>' without 'top', and the directory refusal is framed on the repo root like the git calls that consume the path. Ambient GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS, GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS, GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS and GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS must be unset in both modes. reconcile-manifest-write classifies every path under --literal-pathspecs, devkit reconcile reads the same manifest paths literally, and both scrub ambient pathspec modes through literalPathspecEnv() in reconcile-manifest-write.mts. Raw PATHS stays the storage and display identity, so receipts recorded before the literal-path change still resume.

devkit own test processes inherit NO run authority from whatever launched them. vitest.setup.mjs deletes an explicit, named list of ship/review authority variables before any test module loads (setupFiles runs per worker ahead of the first import, so even a top-level process.env capture sees the cleaned env), and both vitest configs share that one file. A test asserts that vitest.e2e.config.mjs uses the same setupFiles, so the sharing is pinned rather than assumed. The list, SCRUBBED_ENV, is the union of three provenance lists: INHERITED_RUN_ENV, the vocabulary cli/lib/ship/review-target.sh unsets, bound to it by a parity test so the two can never drift (membership is reused, the reason is not: that script prevents inheriting a FOREIGN run authority at a review entrypoint, not in the downstream tree); SHIP_EXPORTED_ENV, the DEVKIT_SHIP_* names ship-branch.sh exports beyond that vocabulary; and TEST_ONLY_ADDITIONS, the FRINK_AI_STRICT alias. review-target.sh's vocabulary alone is never treated as the full scrub list: it is not a superset of what a ship exports, and an inherited DEVKIT_SHIP_ROOT or DEVKIT_SHIP_BRANCH makes a test answer for the OUTER ship's repository. Ship-export coverage is bound at the source, not to a hand-written list: a test parses the export left-hand sides out of ship-branch.sh and run-gates-with-capture.sh and requires every DEVKIT_/GUARD_ name found there to be in SCRUBBED_ENV, so a new ship export must be added to the scrub before it can flip a gate test. Deliberate invocation knobs are never scrubbed: SHIP_COMMIT_TIMEOUT and DEVKIT_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT are inputs a caller chose. A test that needs a policy var sets it explicitly. The guarantee is about INHERITANCE, not visibility - a per-worker setup file cannot undo a test that sets a var mid-file and never restores it.
